events.title: Wild Roots Learning Community
events.description: Wild Roots Learning Community 📅 Dates: Sep. 10, Sep. 24, Oct. 8, Oct. 22, Nov. 12, Dec. 10 (all Thursdays) ⏰ Time: 10:00am-12:00pm (each time) 👧 Age Range: 3-12 y/o (younger/older siblings welcome!) 💵 Cost: $5/kid 3-and-older ⭐ FREE for MDC Members, kids 2-and-under, and accompanying grown-ups Wild Roots is a play-based learning group where kids discover the world around them through child-led exploration. This year, we’re exploring forces—wind, gravity, water, weight, and balance. A little wild. A little wobbly. A whole lot of wonder. 🔎✨ Potential weekly activities include making kites, building giant marble runs, testing boats in MDC’s outdoor pond, creating snow forts, building walkable bridges, and more. But the plan is always flexible. We bring the materials, give starting guidance, and provide encouragement, but the kids’ natural curiosity, burgeoning initiative, and trial-and-error problem solving skills bring the activities to life. Sessions may take place indoors or outdoors, so please ensure you and your kids wear/bring appropriate clothing—even once snow falls! ☀️❄️ Grown-ups are required to supervise their kids, but they get in free! 🪁 Session 1 (September 10) — Kites: Designing, building, and racing kites to see whose creations will catch the wind. Spoiler: Not every kite flies on the first try—and that’s the best part. 💨 Session 2 (September 24) — Pinwheels & Windsocks: Creating a field full of homemade pinwheels and windsocks. Kids get to redesign and relaunch anything that didn’t fly quite right the first time. More session topics will be announced as the season goes on!

events.title: Ursa Minor Oktoberfest Block Print Night
events.description: Ursa Minor Oktoberfest Block Printing Night Thursday, September 24th, 2026 | 4-6:00 PM at Ursa Minor Brewing Looking for a creative night out to kick off Ursa Minor’s Oktoberfest week? Whether you’re hoping to drink great beer, connect with other nature and craft lovers, plan a girls’ evening, enjoy a unique date night, or just want to make something awesome without the sweat of carving and cleanup? We’ve got you covered! Join Anna from Wild Kidd Design for a fun and relaxed DIY block printing session paired with your favorite local beer at Ursa Minor Brewing. Cost: $30 per person (includes one bandana OR tote & access to all block prints) $5 for each additional bandana or print project Pay $30 here to reserve your spot, any additional projects will be paid for at the door. What to Expect: Arrive at 4 PM (event wraps up at 6 PM) Choose from 60+ hand-carved block prints inspired by nature, wildlife and the North Woods vibe – there will also be 5 Oktoberfest and Ursa Minor themed blocks to choose from to ring in the festivities! Select from 2-3 bandana and tote color options, then mix, match, and stamp to your heart’s content Want to get extra creative? Bring your own t-shirt, tote bag, or fabric item to print on too! Space is Limited – Reserve Your Spot! We’re capping the event at 20 people per time slot to make sure everyone gets the space and materials they need. Get your ticket to guarantee your spot! Walk-ins welcome only if space allows, with the best chance of getting in during the second half of the event. If you do not sign up I can not guarantee a spot for you but will try to fit you once those who have signed up finish their projects. Refunds will only be given if you reach out 8 days prior to the event. Come for the crafting, stay for the beer, and leave with a one-of-a-kind creation (or three)! Can’t wait to print with you! Feel free to email any questions (or last minute cancellations) to artkiddstudio@gmail.com Excited to see you there!

events.title: Objects of War: A Storytelling Circle of Service, Memory, and Community
events.description: Veterans Memorial Hall, a program of the St. Louis County Historical Society, is partnering with the Minnesota Humanities Center to present Objects of War: A Storytelling Circle of Service, Memory, and Community on Thursday, September 24, from 6:00 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. at American Legion Post 71. The event is free, and advance registration is required. Register online at https://www.mnhum.org/event/duluth-objects-of-war-a-storytelling-circle-of-service-memory-community. Space is limited, and registration helps organizers plan seating and the light meal. For Objects of War, participants are invited to bring an item connected to military service or the experience of war and conflict — such as dog tags, a service member’s good luck charm, a photograph, a letter, or a family heirloom — and share the story behind it. Guided by trained facilitators, the evening will explore why we hold on to certain objects and how those objects help us better understand the human impacts of war. Participants should come prepared to share a story, listen to others, and enjoy a light meal together. See our website post for complete details: https://www.thehistorypeople.org/single-post/objects-of-war-a-storytelling-circle-of-service-memory-and-community.

events.title: HECK OF THE NORTH & CASTLE DANGER BREWERY PRESENT: CHARLIE PARR
events.description: HECK FEST ABOUT HECK FEST After conquering the gravel roads of Minnesota’s North Shore, join us in downtown Two Harbors for the inaugural Heck Fest, the official post-race celebration of the Heck of the North. Enjoy food trucks, fresh Castle Danger beer, and the camaraderie that makes the Heck of the North community so special. We’re also thrilled to welcome acclaimed Minnesota musician Charlie Parr for a special live performance at 4:00 PM. A longtime favorite of Heck of the North, Charlie’s authentic blend of folk, blues, and Americana provides the perfect soundtrack for an afternoon of celebrating riders, volunteers, and another unforgettable day on the bike. Open to riders, supporters, and the public. Free to attend. ABOUT CHARLIE PARR In the music of Charlie Parr, there is a sincere conviction and earnest drive to create. The Minnesota-born guitarist, songwriter, and interpreter of traditional music has released 19 albums over two decades and has been known to perform up to 275 shows a year. Parr is a folk troubadour in the truest sense: taking to the road between shows, writing and rewriting songs as he plays, fueled by a belief that music is eternal and cannot be claimed or adequately explained. The bluesman poet pulls closely from the sights and sounds around him, his lyrical craftsmanship built by his influences. The sounds from his working-class upbringing—including Folkways legends such as Lead Belly and Woody Guthrie—imbue Parr’s music with stylistic echoes of blues and folk icons of decades past. Parr sees himself merely as a continuer of a folk tradition: “I feel like I stand on a lot of big shoulders,” he said in an interview. “I hope that I’ve brought a little bit of myself to the music.” With a discography simultaneously transcendental in nature and grounded in roots music, Charlie Parr is the humble master of the 21st century folk tradition. events.title: Senior Go Show
events.description: The Show for those 55+ that are Getting Older, but Still GOing! Today’s generation of seniors isn’t the butterscotch in their pocket, tissue in their sleeve seniors of the old days. Today’s seniors and soon-to-be seniors are active, they are still: working, having fun, helping raise their children’s children, vacationing, crafting, building, buying – they are Still Going. And the GO Show will help them find the information they need to get there. At the GO Show, you’ll still find all the important information you need as you get older – estate planning, healthcare, etc – but now the GO Show will focus not just on what you have to do, but what they WANT to do! This means more fun – with exhibitors featuring travel, beer, food, outdoor gear, hobbies, and afternoon entertainment that will rock. We’re excited to meet the needs of today’s seniors and to present an expo where they can enjoy entertainment, gather information, and meet new friends in a festive atmosphere. 70+ vendors ready to showcase products, services, and resources for today’s active seniors. Attendees can enjoy a full day of information, entertainment, and inspiration—absolutely free. Thanks to the generous support of Medica, free parking will be available. FREE tickets are available at most exhibitor locations, Park State Bank locations, Mediqwest and area Essentia Pharmacies while supplies last. If you did not take advantage of getting a free ticket in advance, tickets will be $5 at the door! For more information, visit: www.goshowexpo.com or call 218-727-1177.

events.title: Sketches of Minnesota: Iron Range
events.description: Join the Minnesota Humanities Center, Danger Boat Productions, and Iron Range community for the Sketches of Minnesota civic improv comedy tour at MDC! These free events use laughter and comedy to celebrate Minnesota communities, promote dialogue, bridge divides, and help find ways to work constructively across differences in today’s political environment. Beginning with a free catered meal, these gatherings invite audience members to share what makes their town great, what they think people get wrong about it, what local divisions concern them, and what future they imagine. An improv comedy troupe listens in on the conversations, takes everything they heard from residents, and brings it to life on stage through entirely unscripted improv comedy theater. ⭐ This event is free, however registration is required. Register here. ❓ Registration Questions: registrations@mnhum.org 5:00–6:00pm: Doors open / Community hour 6:00–7:15pm: Dinner 7:15–8:00pm: Improv show 8:00–8:30pm: Talkback Host Partners: Chisholm Community Foundation and Hibbing Foundation The work of the Minnesota Humanities Center is to create a stronger Minnesota by increasing our understanding of the beauty, wisdom and stories of its people. Through partnerships, we facilitate the spaces, like Sketches of Minnesota, that seek to build connections and deepen understanding of ourselves and our communities in pursuit of a more just society. This event is made possible by the generous support of the Saint Paul & Minnesota Foundation.

events.title: Coffee & Colors Sunrise Cruise
events.description: Experience a fall morning on Lake Superior aboard Vista Fleet’s Coffee & Colors Cruise! Hop aboard the Vista Queen in time to catch Duluth’s iconic sunrise from the water, then take in the vibrant fall colors along the Northland’s hillsides. Along the way, learn about the Duluth-Superior Harbor, local history, the science and ecology of the St. Louis River system, and the area’s unique and historic bridges. Complimentary coffee and breakfast pastries are included, making this the perfect way to start a crisp fall day in Duluth. This cruise features open seating. Please note that the Vista Queen is not wheelchair accessible.

events.title: Room for Grief
events.description: A Peer-led gathering on Loss, Grief, & Belonging Paula Williams will hold the space for these peer-led gatherings. Paula is a long-time member of the Northland community having first come to the area in the late 90’s to live and work with the Loaves and Fishes community, then moving to a nearby farm in 2000 where she tried her hand as a flower farmer and hosted gatherings in the big red dairy barn. Motherhood settled her in to life in the country, until she moved back to Duluth in 2024. Paula has worked as a life coach for over 20 years, pivoting to therapy in May. She has been imagining this kind of monthly grief gathering for years and is grateful to Halcyon House for the opportunity to gather in its unique space. Free Event. If you pre-register, we can get an idea of the group size. Otherwise, drop in!

events.title: Duluth River Train Excursion
events.description: Ride the Lake Superior and Mississippi Railroad. A historic 2-hour rail journey through the majestic St. Louis River Estuary. Family-friendly, volunteer-run, and purely Duluth. Our narrated tour takes you along the original Lake Superior & Mississippi line in vintage coaches. Go where cars and hiking boots can’t reach. The St. Louis River Estuary is a hidden sanctuary for bald eagles, osprey, and Northland wildlife. Bring your camera for unparalleled views of the Duluth riverfront. Best to arrive about a half-hour before departure. Our ticket office is located just off of Grand Avenue.

events.description: Called “achingly beautiful, thought-provoking, powerful and prophetic” by Newsday, Anaïs Mitchell’s haunting, jazz-inflected folk opera delivers a deeply resonant and defiantly hopeful theatrical experience. Following two intertwining love stories – that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of immortal King Hades and lady Persephone – Hadestown invites audiences on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Inspired by traditions of classic American folk music and vintage New Orleans jazz, Mitchell’s beguiling sung-through musical pits industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love.

events.title: “The Librarians” Documentary Screening
events.description: Please join the Kathryn A. Martin Library for a screening of the documentary, The Librarians, as well as a banned books discussion panel. Located in Bohannon Hall 90 on the UMD Campus. ABOUT THE FILM Librarians emerge as first responders in the fight for democracy and our First Amendment Rights. As they well know, controlling the flow of ideas means control over communities. In Texas, the Krause List targets 850 books focused on race and LGBTQIA+ stories – triggering sweeping book bans across the U.S. at an unprecedented rate. As tensions escalate, librarians connect the dots from heated school and library board meetings nationwide to lay bare the underpinnings of a large-scale coordinated extremist movement fueling the censorship efforts. Despite facing harassment, threats, and laws aimed at criminalizing their work – the librarians’ rallying cry for freedom to read is a chilling cautionary tale. Runtime: 88 min. Free

events.title: Book Signing: “Perseverance: A Memoir” by Mark Dayton
events.address: 3713 Split Rock Lighthouse Rd., Two Harbors, MN
events.description: Join former governor Mark Dayton for a signing of his memoir Perseverance with a foreword by Hillary Rodham Clinton. In his own words, Perseverance: A Memoir details Dayton’s life story, including his childhood in a dysfunctional household, his political awakening, his early life in politics, and his friendship with Senator Paul Wellstone, whose call, “We all do better when we all do better,” served as a lodestar for Dayton’s ongoing work. The book ends with a postscript on our current moment in public life. In addition to providing an enduring record of recent political history, Dayton’s memoir offers case studies of problems being remedied swiftly under leadership motivated by empathy. Perseverance provides occasion for conversations of consequence and substance, today and for years to come. Mark Dayton served two terms as the fortieth governor of Minnesota, from 2011 to 2019. His other elected offices include state auditor and US senator. Get your copy of the book signed and meet Mark Dayton. Books will be available for purchase.

events.title: Wild Roots Learning Community
events.description: Wild Roots Learning Community 📅 Dates: Sep. 10, Sep. 24, Oct. 8, Oct. 22, Nov. 12, Dec. 10 (all Thursdays) ⏰ Time: 10:00am-12:00pm (each time) 👧 Age Range: 3-12 y/o (younger/older siblings welcome!) 💵 Cost: $5/kid 3-and-older ⭐ FREE for MDC Members, kids 2-and-under, and accompanying grown-ups Wild Roots is a play-based learning group where kids discover the world around them through child-led exploration. This year, we’re exploring forces—wind, gravity, water, weight, and balance. A little wild. A little wobbly. A whole lot of wonder. 🔎✨ Potential weekly activities include making kites, building giant marble runs, testing boats in MDC’s outdoor pond, creating snow forts, building walkable bridges, and more. But the plan is always flexible. We bring the materials, give starting guidance, and provide encouragement, but the kids’ natural curiosity, burgeoning initiative, and trial-and-error problem solving skills bring the activities to life. Sessions may take place indoors or outdoors, so please ensure you and your kids wear/bring appropriate clothing—even once snow falls! ☀️❄️ Grown-ups are required to supervise their kids, but they get in free! 🪁 Session 1 (September 10) — Kites: Designing, building, and racing kites to see whose creations will catch the wind. Spoiler: Not every kite flies on the first try—and that’s the best part. 💨 Session 2 (September 24) — Pinwheels & Windsocks: Creating a field full of homemade pinwheels and windsocks. Kids get to redesign and relaunch anything that didn’t fly quite right the first time. More session topics will be announced as the season goes on!

events.title: Rock From the Heart
events.description: A Benefit Concert for Aortic Health Awareness Rock from the Heart brings the music—and the mission—together for a night of high-energy rock and real impact. Arch Allies will deliver the legendary sounds of Styx, Journey, REO Speedwagon, and more, while Rock from the Heart’s own house band, Aortic Fire, brings a performance that hits close to home. Together, it’s a full night of arena-style rock with a purpose. This event is part of Rock from the Heart’s ongoing work to raise awareness and provide education around aortic and heart valve disease—conditions that often go undetected until it’s too late. Through music, shared stories, and community connection, we’re helping people better understand their risk, know their family history, and feel supported every step of the way. 5pm – Rockin Heart’s preshow party (for those who purchase the Rockin’ Hearts or Ultimate Experience tickets) 7pm – Doors Doors (for those who purchase General Admission and Reserved Table Seating) 8pm – Benefit Concert ABOUT ROCK FROM THE HEART Rock from the Heart’s mission is to proactively educate people about aortic and heart valve disease, bridge the gap between impacted families and the support they need, connect those diagnosed with vital resources, and inspire all through the healing power of music. Visit for more info: rockfromtheheart.org

events.title: Photography & Art at the Rock: Featuring Shawn Malone
events.address: 3713 Split Rock Lighthouse Rd., Two Harbors, MN
events.description: September at the Rock celebrates the wonder of Lake Superior—by day, by night, and under the stars. We are proud to feature Shawn Malone, a landscape photographer and visual artist whose work has been inspired by the Lake Superior region for more than 25 years. After moving from Chicago to Marquette, Michigan, Shawn found both her home and her artistic calling along the shores of Lake Superior. Since then, she has dedicated her career to capturing the ever-changing beauty of this remarkable landscape—from rugged coastlines and dramatic weather to the brilliant colors of the aurora borealis and the quiet brilliance of the night sky. Best known for her immersive aurora and night sky photography, Shawn creates images and time-lapse films that reveal the beauty of the natural world in ways often hidden from the naked eye. Her work invites viewers to slow down, look up, and experience the wonder that unfolds after sunset. In addition to operating her Lake Superior Photo gallery in downtown Marquette, Shawn is an award-winning photographer, educator, and workshop leader. She has spent more than a decade sharing her passion for the night sky through presentations, photography workshops, and guided experiences throughout the Great Lakes region, helping others discover the magic of photographing Lake Superior under the stars. On display September 1–30. Meet the Artist: September 29 | 10 am–6 pm Experience Lake Superior through the lens of one of the region’s most accomplished night sky photographers.

events.title: Pumpkin Hunt at the Library
events.description: Mark your calendars for a Pumpkin Hunt on Saturday, October 10, at 10am, exclusively at the Downtown Duluth Public Library location. We’re teaming up with Lake Superior Art Glass to reward pumpkin hunters with tiny glass pumpkins, handmade right here in Duluth. This year’s hunt will feature clues associated with banned books, in celebration of National Banned Books Week October 4-10, 2026. This year’s pumpkin hunt clues will be geared towards the adults, but there will be something special for the kids, too! A fall-themed treasure box will be available for children to hunt for their own mini treasures while the adults match up their clues with the correct banned book to earn their very own handmade glass pumpkin as a prize. So round up your pumpkin hunt search party, and make plans to spend your Saturday morning on October 10 at the Downtown Duluth Public Library location in search of pumpkins and fall mini treasures. We can’t wait to see you there!

events.title: Duluth River Train Excursion

The St. Louis River Estuary is a hidden sanctuary for bald eagles, osprey, and Northland wildlife. Bring your camera for unparalleled views of the Duluth riverfront. Best to arrive about a half-hour before departure. Our ticket office is located just off of Grand Avenue.

events.title: Lunch & Leaves Cruise on the Vista Fleet
events.description: Experience fall in Duluth from the water aboard Vista Fleet’s Lunch & Leaves Cruise! Take in the beautiful fall colors of the Northland while enjoying a relaxing cruise aboard the Vista Star and a delicious lunch from MidCoast Catering. Choose from a Turkey, Bacon & Swiss sandwich with cranberry mayo, lettuce and tomato; a Ham & Provolone Croissant with lettuce and tomato; or a Hummus Wrap with zucchini, squash, roasted red peppers, spinach and hummus. Each lunch is served with Cream of Wild Rice soup, chips and dessert. Along the way, enjoy narrated highlights about the Duluth-Superior Harbor, the science and ecology of the St. Louis River system, and the area’s unique and historic bridges. Space is limited, so reserve your spot and enjoy one of the best ways to experience fall in Duluth!

The legendary tale of Swan Lake takes flight in a breathtaking production from World Ballet Company, as fate and magic entwine in a timeless battle between good and evil. Performing with a Live Orchestra, and featuring a cast of 50 international dancers, over 150 radiant hand-sewn costumes, and stunning hand-crafted sets, this spellbinding ballet captures every heart-pounding moment – from the Dance of the Little Swans to the Black Swan’s 32 fouettés, and every pirouette in between. With Tchaikovsky’s unforgettable score soaring through the air and played LIVE, immerse yourself in this mesmerizing journey where dreams, heartbreak, and hope unfold right before your eyes. Duration: 2 hours 30 minutes (including 20-minute intermission) Audience: For ages 5 & over ABOUT WORLD BALLET COMPANY World Ballet Company – Ballet Everywhere, Ballet For All. Based in Los Angeles, and led by Sasha Gorskaya and Gulya Hartwick, World Ballet Company presents the most beloved and iconic ballets of our time in cities nationwide. Driven by the belief that ballet is for everyone, performances appeal to newcomers and seasoned ballet goers alike. The company attracts many international artists and comprises renowned professional dancers representing over ten countries. events.description: Hadestown, previously scheduled for March 16, 2026, at the DECC Symphony Hall, has been POSTPONED due to travel conditions and restrictions surrounding the Midwest Winter Storm. The performance has been rescheduled for Monday, October 19, 2026. All current tickets will be valid for the October performance. ABOUT THE SHOW COME SEE HOW THE WORLD COULD BE. Welcome to HADESTOWN, where a song can change your fate. Winner of eight 2019 Tony Awards® including Best Musical and the 2020 Grammy® Award for Best Musical Theater Album, this acclaimed new show from celebrated singer-songwriter Anaïs Mitchell and original director Rachel Chavkin (Natasha, Pierre & The Great Comet of 1812) is a love story for today... and always. HADESTOWN intertwines two mythic tales — that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of King Hades and his wife Persephone — as it invites you on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Mitchell’s beguiling melodies and Chavkin’s poetic imagination pit industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love. Performed by a vibrant ensemble of actors, dancers and singers, HADESTOWN is a haunting and hopeful theatrical experience that grabs you and never lets go. events.title: Antique Appraisal
events.description: Bring your antique/collectible item for a free appraisal to the St. Louis County Depot at 506 West Michigan Street, Duluth, Minnesota. The St. Louis County Historical Society has arranged for Denny Mager of Northern Specialty, an expert in antique appraisal, to be at your service beginning at noon in the Union Lounge (outside of the Board Room), which is on street level. Follow event signage. Registration is in person only and cut-off at 2:30PM, so the appraiser can finish appraisals by 3PM. Guests are called up in the order that they are registered. You may bring up to two items per person for an informal oral identification and evaluation of each antique. If the piece is too large or fragile to be hand-carried, clear photographs with a description of any marks and labels will be sufficient. Past participants have thoroughly enjoyed the appraiser’s comments on what is always an interesting assortment of antiques and collectibles. This session is part of an on-going public education program offered by the St. Louis County Historical Society. Sponsorship does not imply endorsement of this or any other estate/appraisal service, and museum staff members are prohibited by professional ethics from making financial appraisals.

events.title: Danny Frank & The Smoky Gold album release concert
events.description: Duluth-based Americana group Danny Frank & The Smoky Gold celebrate the release of their new album “Dedication.” Steeped in musical traditions of folk, bluegrass, country, classic rock, and blues, Danny Frank & The Smoky Gold offers a genre-blending sound that is captivating, invigorating, and sure to get your toe tapping. After two decades of writing songs and performing as a solo artist, Danny Frank released of his debut album “Smoky Gold” in 2021. He then assembled an all-star cast of seasoned musicians to fully compliment his music. “The Smoky Gold” is comprised of banjo player Harrison Olk (Tin Can Gin, Cascade Crescendo, Kind Country Band), bassist Joe Scarpellino (Smokin’ Joe, Dead Larry), and fiddle savant Erin Aldridge (Concert Master – Duluth Superior Symphony Orchestra). Together the group has recorded and released the full length album “Dedication.” Opening the evening will be Adam Greuel (Horseshoes & Hand Grenades) and Kenny Leiser (Joseph Huber). Advance e-tickets will go on sale for $20 (plus $3.18 in fees) at 10 a.m. Friday, Sept. 11 on Eventbrite HERE. Paper tickets will be available at Globe News in Superior for $20 (cash only) and Zenith Bookstore in West Duluth for $20 (plus $1 handling fee). Tickets will be available at the door for $25 while supply lasts. Doors at 6 :30 pm. Music at 7:30.

events.title: Wild Roots Learning Community
events.description: Wild Roots Learning Community 📅 Dates: Sep. 10, Sep. 24, Oct. 8, Oct. 22, Nov. 12, Dec. 10 (all Thursdays) ⏰ Time: 10:00am-12:00pm (each time) 👧 Age Range: 3-12 y/o (younger/older siblings welcome!) 💵 Cost: $5/kid 3-and-older ⭐ FREE for MDC Members, kids 2-and-under, and accompanying grown-ups Wild Roots is a play-based learning group where kids discover the world around them through child-led exploration. This year, we’re exploring forces—wind, gravity, water, weight, and balance. A little wild. A little wobbly. A whole lot of wonder. 🔎✨ Potential weekly activities include making kites, building giant marble runs, testing boats in MDC’s outdoor pond, creating snow forts, building walkable bridges, and more. But the plan is always flexible. We bring the materials, give starting guidance, and provide encouragement, but the kids’ natural curiosity, burgeoning initiative, and trial-and-error problem solving skills bring the activities to life. Sessions may take place indoors or outdoors, so please ensure you and your kids wear/bring appropriate clothing—even once snow falls! ☀️❄️ Grown-ups are required to supervise their kids, but they get in free! 🪁 Session 1 (September 10) — Kites: Designing, building, and racing kites to see whose creations will catch the wind. Spoiler: Not every kite flies on the first try—and that’s the best part. 💨 Session 2 (September 24) — Pinwheels & Windsocks: Creating a field full of homemade pinwheels and windsocks. Kids get to redesign and relaunch anything that didn’t fly quite right the first time. More session topics will be announced as the season goes on!

events.title: History Happy Hour
events.description: Step into the 1920s for an evening of cocktails, hors d’oeuvres, music, and history at Glensheen! Begin your evening by entering through the Juliet Balcony, where you’ll be greeted with a cocktail and hors d’oeuvres before heading downstairs to explore Glensheen’s basement. Discover 1920s-inspired activities and artifacts on display, enjoy music from the era, snap a photo in the billiards room, and take in a few surprises along the way. Enjoy a selection of fun, 1920s-inspired cocktails available for purchase at the cash bar before settling in for an engaging history talk by local historian Tony Dierckins. Tony will present “Drying Out Duluth: From Temperance to Prohibition,” exploring Duluth’s complicated relationship with alcohol—from the city’s early liquor ordinances and temperance movement to Prohibition and the creative ways Duluthians continued to enjoy a drink. Following the talk, enjoy dessert and a special 1920s-themed experience to round out the evening. Dress to impress and embrace the spirit of the 1920s for this one-of-a-kind night at Glensheen. This event is for guests ages 21 and older. Doors open at 5:30 p.m. | Talk begins at 6:30 p.m. | Event ends at 9 p.m. Tickets: $45 Members | $55 Non-Members Purchase tickets at z.umn.edu/historyhappyhour

events.description: Organist Aaron David Miller accompanies the classic 1920 silent horror film “The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari.” The Friends of The Felgemaker invite you to experience what it was like to attend a silent movie! Renowned organist Aaron David Miller will accompany the silent film “The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari” at 7 p.m. Friday, Oct. 23 on the historic Felgemaker pipe organ housed at Sacred Heart Music Center. “The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari” is a groundbreaking German horror film which set standards for creative camera work and featured a dark and twisted style of storytelling. It is widely considered the first true horror story put to film. Aaron David Miller is noted for his highly imaginative and creative style, found in his performances, improvisations and compositions. He has won numerous international awards for improvisation and has given concerts and accompanied silent films across the country. events.title: Ghost in the Gallery
events.venue: Richard I. Bong Veterans Historical Center
events.description: Ghosts in the Bong Center Museum Galleries! This Halloween season, the Bong Veterans Museum invites you to experience our museum in a whole new light. On October 24th, you can alter your vision and get spooky if you choose. The galleries will take on a mysterious atmosphere; visitors of all ages are welcome to wander through exhibits where history and imagination blur. Our mannequins have always stood watch, but during this special event you may find yourself asking—are they moving, or is it just the season playing tricks on you? Families can enjoy a mild, sensory-friendly adventure designed to spark curiosity without ever overwhelming younger visitors. For those who prefer a gentler experience, accommodations will be made to ensure everyone can participate at their own comfort level. This isn’t a haunted house—it’s a chance to celebrate the spooky season in a unique, educational, and welcoming environment. Discover the secrets of our mannequins, share in the fun of Halloween with your loved ones, and see the Bong Center like you’ve never seen it before. Regular admission applies.

events.title: Neural Exercises for Autism, a conversation with the author
events.venue: At Sara's Table Chester Creek Cafe
events.description: Is Autism an identity or a disorder, is an ongoing question which faces those who describe themselves under the umbrella of Neurodiversity language. WW Norton author, and autistic individual, Sean Inderbitzen LCSW, DSW, invites neurodiverse Duluthians to wrestle with this question with him in a small gathering setting. Themes to be covered from his new book in this talk include identity, temperment, disorder, empathy, and the role of ambiguous loss in shaping connection and rigidity. These themes like these and more appear in his new book Neural Exercises for Autism, and we invite you to meet with the author partaking in discussion, pastries, and a dive into meaning and neurodiversity. Please register for our gathering complete with readings, discussion, pastries from Sara’s Table at Chester Creek Cafe, and Alcoholic beverages available for purchase. Pastries will be provided for those who wish to partake, and beverages are guest responsibility. Our event is on a first come first serve basis. If you are unable to make it and register, please cancel as space is limited to the first 25 registrations.

Ryan will be reading from his latest poetry collection, The Cave, which explores the topics of fatherhood, generational trauma, and the ways place and lineage connect. It has been named one of the “Best Poetry Books of 2025” by the California Review of Books and “Top 5 of 2025” by Zenith Bookstore in Duluth, MN. Ryan was born and raised on the backwaters of the St. Louis River in the Fond Du Lac neighborhood of western Duluth. Along with being a poet, he is also a professor of English at the College of St. Scholastica. His honors include the Northeastern Minnesota Book Award, the Weldon Kees Award, the Robert Watson Poetry Prize, and more. Here’s the evening’s schedule: 🥂 5:00pm: Mingling and (free!) snacks (first-come, first-served) 🗣️ 6:00pm: The poetry reading begins ✒️ 6:45pm: Ryan signs books 👋 7:30pm: We say goodnight Take a look at these reviews of The Cave: “While the poems in The Cave are thoroughly contemporary, many of their philosophical underpinnings are as old as humanity itself. Vine’s haunting meditations on fatherhood, for example, are as profound and enduring as any I’ve ever read. I learned stuff I never knew before – and I was there!” Peter Asher, Grammy-Winning Producer/Artist/Manager and Sirius XM Radio Host In Deconstructing The Music LIVE: Pink Floyd’s The Dark Side of the Moon, Scott Freiman, host of the Public Television series Deconstructing the Beatles, celebrates Pink Floyd’s groundbreaking 1973 album with his first non-Beatles “deconstruction.” Scott will take you on a track-by-track journey through this Pink Floyd masterpiece, explaining the inspiration for the songs and their evolution in the studio. Dark Side of the Moon is a concept album that explores themes of life, death, time, and the human experience. events.description: Called “achingly beautiful, thought-provoking, powerful and prophetic” by Newsday, Anaïs Mitchell’s haunting, jazz-inflected folk opera delivers a deeply resonant and defiantly hopeful theatrical experience. Following two intertwining love stories – that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of immortal King Hades and lady Persephone – Hadestown invites audiences on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. events.title: City Council Pre-Agenda Meeting
events.description: The 5:00 p.m. pre-agenda meeting is a work session between the City Council and City staff to review the upcoming City Council meeting agenda, future meeting agendas, and is a time for the City Council and City staff to have discussions about the agenda items and asking and answering questions. The agenda for the pre-agenda meeting is the same document as the upcoming City Council meeting agenda but does not follow the same format as the City Council meeting. Although pre-agenda meetings are open to the public, it is not a time for public comment, as the public can listen to the conversation and ask questions or provide input at the upcoming City Council meeting. Visitors should park in the North parking lot and enter Door 6.

events.title: 38 Special
events.description: Thursday, November 5, 2026 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm Presented by Pepper Entertainment TICKETS Tickets on sale now! ABOUT 38 SPECIAL Formed in 1974, the band toured tirelessly from the start, sharpening the explosive live show that’s been 38 Special’s calling card for a half-century. Along the way, the Florida natives fine-tuned their sound too: a blend of muscle and melody, filled with the arena-rock pop hooks that would soon become staples of FM radio. Years passed... trends changed... some band members retired from the rigors... but 38 Special remained, hitting the road year after year, flying the flag for an enduring form of classic rock & roll that never dies. As 38 Special enters its sixth decade together, the music continues with Milestone. It’s the band’s first studio album in more than 20 years, and it showcases a group of road warriors with plenty of miles left in the tank. Fueled up on snarling guitars, anthemic melodies, and the desire to break new ground, they update their sound for the 2020s, bridging the gap between past and present without forgetting their rock & roll roots. “After all this time, we wanted to create a more modern 38 Special album,” says frontman and co-founder Don Barnes. “This is a fresh, updated approach to the sound we’ve been making together for so long. Why not make a big statement after all these years? When you’re reintroducing yourself to the world, ‘good enough’ doesn’t work anymore. If you’re gonna do it, you might as well go big.” Learn more at 38special.com KNOW BEFORE YOU GO

events.description: An Astrophysicist Goes to the Movies – Part I Presented by Roberts Group TICKETS Tickets on sale now! ABOUT THE SHOW “An Astrophysicist Goes to the Movies – Part I” From Star Wars to Armageddon to Titanic to The Martian to oddly scientifically literate Beer Commercials. An entertaining and enlightening review of all the science that our favorite movies got wrong, combined with some of the stuff they got right. Incorporates recent films as well as some classics that you may not have known had any science in them at all. ABOUT NEIL DEGRASSE TYSON Neil deGrasse Tyson was born and raised in New York City where he was educated in the public schools clear through his graduation from the Bronx High School of Science. Tyson went on to earn his BA in Physics from Harvard and his PhD in Astrophysics from Columbia. In 2001, Tyson was appointed by President Bush to serve on a twelve-member commission that studied the Future of the U.S. Aerospace Industry. The final report was published in 2002 and contained recommendations (for Congress and for the major agencies of the government) that would promote a thriving future of transportation, space exploration, and national security. In 2004, Tyson was once again appointed by President Bush to serve on a nine-member commission on the Implementation of the United States Space Exploration Policy, dubbed the “Moon, Mars, and Beyond” commission. This group navigated a path by which the new space vision can become a successful part of the American agenda. And in 2006, the head of NASA appointed Tyson to serve on its prestigious Advisory Council, which guides NASA through its perennial need to fit ambitious visions into restricted budgets. In addition to dozens of professional publications, Dr. Tyson has written, and continues to write for the public. events.title: Edmund Fitzgerald: A Great Lakes Memorial
events.address: 3713 Split Rock Lighthouse Rd., Two Harbors, MN
events.description: This annual event commemorates the sinking of the freighter Edmund Fitzgerald and the total loss of the 29 crew members aboard on November 10, 1975. It is also a time to reflect on the memory of all lives lost on the Great Lakes. The lighthouse, fog signal building, and visitor center will be open for visitors. Guides will welcome visitors and provide historic site and shipwreck information. Throughout the day, visitors can watch a film about Edmund Fitzgerald in the visitor center, or join a guided tour exploring the history of Fitzgerald’s final voyage. At 4:15 pm, the lighthouse will temporarily close while the names of the crew are read to the tolling of a ship’s bell, with a rendition of the Naval Hymn. Following the ceremony, the beacon will be lit, and the tower will be open again to tour until close at 6 pm. Be sure to bring a flashlight or headlamp as the grounds and trails are unlit. The weather is unpredictable, please dress accordingly. The event will be streamed on Split Rock’s Facebook Page and the Minnesota Historical Society’s YouTube channel. Tickets are offered online and onsite. Tickets only guarantee you admission to the site and program. It does not guarantee you a parking space or specific seating at the event.

events.title: Pruitt Center Virtual Speaker: Shawn Achor – The Power of Belief
events.description: Join us for the Pruitt Center Fall 2026 Virtual Speaker, Shawn Achor! Conventional wisdom holds that success is determined by talent, intelligence or the circumstances we happen to land in. After more than a decade of research at Harvard and work in 51 countries, Shawn Achor found that the greatest predictor of our future success is something else entirely: the set of beliefs we hold about the world around us. Beliefs are not passive. They shape what we notice, how we interpret setbacks, how much energy and persistence we bring to hard problems and whether we see a challenge as fixed or changeable. And because beliefs spread through teams the same way emotions do, a single person’s belief about what is possible can raise—or quietly cap—the ceiling for an entire organization. In his newest book, The Power of Beliefs, Shawn demonstrates that these beliefs are far more malleable than we assume, and that changing them is one of the fastest levers we have for changing performance. In his talk, Shawn uses research and case studies to show practical ways individuals and teams can surface the beliefs limiting them, reframe challenges as changeable, expand what they believe is possible and sustain those shifts under pressure. Register here for this virtual event: uwsuper.edu/ShawnAchor Shawn Achor is the NYTimes bestselling author of The Happiness Advantage and The Power of Beliefs. Shawn graduated magna cum laudefrom Harvard and earned a Masters from Harvard Divinity School in Christian and Buddhist ethics. After spending 12 years at Harvard, Shawn traveled to 50 countries studying how to create an interconnected approach to potential and happiness.

events.title: Pruitt Center Virtual Speaker: Shawn Achor – The Power of Belief
events.venue: Virtual on Zoom: Register at uwsuper.edu/ShawnAchor to receive the Zoom link.
events.description: Join us for the Pruitt Center Fall 2026 Virtual Speaker, Shawn Achor! Conventional wisdom holds that success is determined by talent, intelligence or the circumstances we happen to land in. After more than a decade of research at Harvard and work in 51 countries, Shawn Achor found that the greatest predictor of our future success is something else entirely: the set of beliefs we hold about the world around us. Beliefs are not passive. They shape what we notice, how we interpret setbacks, how much energy and persistence we bring to hard problems and whether we see a challenge as fixed or changeable. And because beliefs spread through teams the same way emotions do, a single person’s belief about what is possible can raise—or quietly cap—the ceiling for an entire organization. In his newest book, The Power of Beliefs, Shawn demonstrates that these beliefs are far more malleable than we assume, and that changing them is one of the fastest levers we have for changing performance. In his talk, Shawn uses research and case studies to show practical ways individuals and teams can surface the beliefs limiting them, reframe challenges as changeable, expand what they believe is possible and sustain those shifts under pressure. Register at uwsuper.edu/ShawnAchor

events.description: Wild Roots Learning Community 📅 Dates: Sep. 10, Sep. 24, Oct. 8, Oct. 22, Nov. 12, Dec. 10 (all Thursdays) ⏰ Time: 10:00am-12:00pm (each time) 👧 Age Range: 3-12 y/o (younger/older siblings welcome!) 💵 Cost: $5/kid 3-and-older ⭐ FREE for MDC Members, kids 2-and-under, and accompanying grown-ups Wild Roots is a play-based learning group where kids discover the world around them through child-led exploration. events.description: The 5:00 p.m. pre-agenda meeting is a work session between the City Council and City staff to review the upcoming City Council meeting agenda, future meeting agendas, and is a time for the City Council and City staff to have discussions about the agenda items and asking and answering questions. The agenda for the pre-agenda meeting is the same document as the upcoming City Council meeting agenda but does not follow the same format as the City Council meeting. Antique Appraisal
events.description: Bring your antique/collectible item for a free appraisal to the St. Louis County Depot at 506 West Michigan Street, Duluth, Minnesota. The St. Louis County Historical Society has arranged for Denny Mager of Northern Specialty, an expert in antique appraisal, to be at your service beginning at noon in the Union Lounge (outside of the Board Room), which is on street level. Follow event signage. Registration is in person only and cut-off at 2:30PM, so the appraiser can finish appraisals by 3PM. Guests are called up in the order that they are registered. You may bring up to two items per person for an informal oral identification and evaluation of each antique. If the piece is too large or fragile to be hand-carried, clear photographs with a description of any marks and labels will be sufficient. Past participants have thoroughly enjoyed the appraiser’s comments on what is always an interesting assortment of antiques and collectibles. This session is part of an on-going public education program offered by the St. Louis County Historical Society. Sponsorship does not imply endorsement of this or any other estate/appraisal service, and museum staff members are prohibited by professional ethics from making financial appraisals.

events.title: Mason Jennings
events.description: Minnesota troubadour Mason Jennings returns performing old favorites and work from his new album “Dark Wings.” “I love song craft,” says Mason Jennings, a folksinger who has spent over two decades honing his craft both on stage and in the studio. “A song is like a boat on the water, and you’re trying to make it float with as few pieces as possible. If you do it right, a song can be very healing.” For Jennings, songwriting has always been about a personal connection, both with his audience and himself. He’s known for an unpretentious, emotive approach to folk music, combining introspective lyrics with acoustic melodies. His work has drawn comparisons to genre greats, including Nick Drake, John Fahey, and Tom Waits. But Jennings’ sound is distinctly his own, one that blends vulnerability with strength, simplicity with complexity. That style comes through on his new record: “Dark Wings.” His 18th studio album, the record finds Jennings moving between raw honesty about childhood scars, dark thoughts, spiritual questioning and a stubborn belief in the power of love. Duluth-based singer-songwriter and bandleader Breanne Marie of Breanne Marie & The Front Porch Sinners will open with a solo set. Advance E-tickets are available for $25 (plus $3.52 in fees) on Eventbrite HERE. Paper tickets will be available for $25 at Zenith Bookstore in West Duluth (plus $1 handling fee) and at Globe News in Superior (cash only). Tickets will be available at the door for $30 while supply lasts. Doors at 6:30. Music at 7:30.

events.title: Duluth Winter Village
events.description: THE MAGIC RETURNS TO HARBOR DRIVE! Dates & Times: December 5–6, 2026 | Saturday & Sunday | 10:00 am – 4:00 pm Admission & Parking: FREE to attend! (DECC Parking is $10) AN EVENT UNLIKE ANY OTHER! For one weekend only, we’re bringing together the best of Duluth in one scenic location. The 10th annual Duluth Winter Village returns along the lake on Harbor Drive this December 5 and 6 from 10:00 am – 4:00 pm. The magic of local businesses, charming wooden shopping cabins, family-friendly activities, hot food, beverages (including beer & cocktails), and carolers continues to be a magical tradition. The festivities are held outside and inside at the Duluth Entertainment Convention Center. Visitors will appreciate: Our famous holiday-themed Experiential Bar “Tinsel Tavern” — featuring cocktails from Vikre Distillery Local makers & on-site Blacksmith Soup flights On-site holiday portraits by the Christmas tree Hollybeary Kid Store is back with more shopping options for littles to pick out for their grown-ups Animals, live caroling, 25-foot lit tree Small Children and Nursing Area by Duluth Mom Duluth Winter Village merch produced by our local vendors Hug-a-Hen by the Locally Laid Egg Company Lift Bridge, freighter views and bonfires The annual event began on the grounds of Glensheen Mansion in 2016 but moved to its new location in 2021. The Duluth Winter Village is unique from other area markets in that the vendors are all local businesses with retail locations around Northern Minnesota. Participants include Bailey Builds, Altered Abode, Y-ker Acres, Hucklebeary, Frost River, the Rainbow Room, NaturaLight, The Big Lake, Wintergreen Northern Wear, Lake Superior Art Glass, Ivy Moon and the Moon Market. Food and drink from the DECC’s culinary team, Positively Third Street Bakery, Hungry Hippie Tacos, Duluth’s Best Bread, Love Creamery, Scenic 61 by New Scenic Café, TBSP Waffles, Yes Cheese, and more. For more information, visit here.

events.title: Hadestown: Teen Edition
events.description: Called “achingly beautiful, thought-provoking, powerful and prophetic” by Newsday, Anaïs Mitchell’s haunting, jazz-inflected folk opera delivers a deeply resonant and defiantly hopeful theatrical experience. Following two intertwining love stories – that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of immortal King Hades and lady Persephone – Hadestown invites audiences on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Inspired by traditions of classic American folk music and vintage New Orleans jazz, Mitchell’s beguiling sung-through musical pits industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love.

events.description: The 5:00 p.m. pre-agenda meeting is a work session between the City Council and City staff to review the upcoming City Council meeting agenda, future meeting agendas, and is a time for the City Council and City staff to have discussions about the agenda items and asking and answering questions. The agenda for the pre-agenda meeting is the same document as the upcoming City Council meeting agenda but does not follow the same format as the City Council meeting. Although pre-agenda meetings are open to the public, it is not a time for public comment, as the public can listen to the conversation and ask questions or provide input at the upcoming City Council meeting. Visitors should park in the North parking lot and enter Door 6.

events.title: Wild Roots Learning Community
events.description: Wild Roots Learning Community 📅 Dates: Sep. 10, Sep. 24, Oct. 8, Oct. 22, Nov. 12, Dec. 10 (all Thursdays) ⏰ Time: 10:00am-12:00pm (each time) 👧 Age Range: 3-12 y/o (younger/older siblings welcome!) 💵 Cost: $5/kid 3-and-older ⭐ FREE for MDC Members, kids 2-and-under, and accompanying grown-ups Wild Roots is a play-based learning group where kids discover the world around them through child-led exploration. This year, we’re exploring forces—wind, gravity, water, weight, and balance. A little wild. A little wobbly. A whole lot of wonder. 🔎✨ Potential weekly activities include making kites, building giant marble runs, testing boats in MDC’s outdoor pond, creating snow forts, building walkable bridges, and more. But the plan is always flexible. We bring the materials, give starting guidance, and provide encouragement, but the kids’ natural curiosity, burgeoning initiative, and trial-and-error problem solving skills bring the activities to life. Sessions may take place indoors or outdoors, so please ensure you and your kids wear/bring appropriate clothing—even once snow falls! ☀️❄️ Grown-ups are required to supervise their kids, but they get in free! 🪁 Session 1 (September 10) — Kites: Designing, building, and racing kites to see whose creations will catch the wind. Spoiler: Not every kite flies on the first try—and that’s the best part. 💨 Session 2 (September 24) — Pinwheels & Windsocks: Creating a field full of homemade pinwheels and windsocks. Kids get to redesign and relaunch anything that didn’t fly quite right the first time. More session topics will be announced as the season goes on!

events.title: Retail Employee Day
events.description: Today the City of Proctor proudly recognizes the hardworking team at Mountain Spirits Municipal Liquor Store in honor of Retail Employees’ Day. Retail Employees’ Day celebrates the dedicated people who keep stores running and ensure customers have a positive shopping experience. From helping customers find the perfect bottle, stocking shelves, managing inventory, and keeping the store welcoming and organized, retail employees play an important role in connecting products with the people who enjoy them. At Mountain Spirits, our team works year-round to provide friendly service, maintain a well-stocked store, and support this City or Proctor’s municipal enterprises. Their efforts help make shopping easy, enjoyable, and welcoming for everyone who walks through the door. Please join us in thanking the Mountain Spirits staff for their hard work, professionalism, and commitment to serving the Proctor community. Your dedication does not go unnoticed!

events.title: Hadestown: Teen Edition
events.description: Called “achingly beautiful, thought-provoking, powerful and prophetic” by Newsday, Anaïs Mitchell’s haunting, jazz-inflected folk opera delivers a deeply resonant and defiantly hopeful theatrical experience. Following two intertwining love stories – that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of immortal King Hades and lady Persephone – Hadestown invites audiences on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Inspired by traditions of classic American folk music and vintage New Orleans jazz, Mitchell’s beguiling sung-through musical pits industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love.

events.description: Called “achingly beautiful, thought-provoking, powerful and prophetic” by Newsday, Anaïs Mitchell’s haunting, jazz-inflected folk opera delivers a deeply resonant and defiantly hopeful theatrical experience. Following two intertwining love stories – that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of immortal King Hades and lady Persephone – Hadestown invites audiences on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Inspired by traditions of classic American folk music and vintage New Orleans jazz, Mitchell’s beguiling sung-through musical pits industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love.

The agenda for the pre-agenda meeting is the same document as the upcoming City Council meeting agenda but does not follow the same format as the City Council meeting. Although pre-agenda meetings are open to the public, it is not a time for public comment, as the public can listen to the conversation and ask questions or provide input at the upcoming City Council meeting. events.title: Hadestown: Teen Edition
events.description: Called “achingly beautiful, thought-provoking, powerful and prophetic” by Newsday, Anaïs Mitchell’s haunting, jazz-inflected folk opera delivers a deeply resonant and defiantly hopeful theatrical experience. Following two intertwining love stories – that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of immortal King Hades and lady Persephone – Hadestown invites audiences on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Inspired by traditions of classic American folk music and vintage New Orleans jazz, Mitchell’s beguiling sung-through musical pits industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love.

events.description: Called “achingly beautiful, thought-provoking, powerful and prophetic” by Newsday, Anaïs Mitchell’s haunting, jazz-inflected folk opera delivers a deeply resonant and defiantly hopeful theatrical experience. Following two intertwining love stories – that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of immortal King Hades and lady Persephone – Hadestown invites audiences on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Inspired by traditions of classic American folk music and vintage New Orleans jazz, Mitchell’s beguiling sung-through musical pits industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love.

events.title: High Key Mondays & Industry Nights
events.description: High Key Mondays & Industry Night Are BACK! Live local music | Drink specials | 6–9pm High Key Monday is FRI-YAY for many of our industry partners — and we’re roll with it. Calling all restaurant, bar, liquor store, and brewery professionals in the Twin Ports — get on down to the Paddle for Industry Night! Show a worker ID or pay stub for $1 off all Bent Paddle beverages. Thank you for keeping our paddles in the water! Everyone is welcome! Come for the tunes, stay for the conversations, delicious beverages, and good times. This month to kick off and celebrate the return, we invite you to connect with local organizations making waves in the Twin Ports — like WE Health, Trans+ Northland, Twin Ports Artists Collective, and Men As Peacemakers. Org’s may vary based on who available each week, but the good vibes are guaranteed!

events.description: Called “achingly beautiful, thought-provoking, powerful and prophetic” by Newsday, Anaïs Mitchell’s haunting, jazz-inflected folk opera delivers a deeply resonant and defiantly hopeful theatrical experience. Following two intertwining love stories – that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of immortal King Hades and lady Persephone – Hadestown invites audiences on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Inspired by traditions of classic American folk music and vintage New Orleans jazz, Mitchell’s beguiling sung-through musical pits industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love.

events.description: Called “achingly beautiful, thought-provoking, powerful and prophetic” by Newsday, Anaïs Mitchell’s haunting, jazz-inflected folk opera delivers a deeply resonant and defiantly hopeful theatrical experience. Following two intertwining love stories – that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of immortal King Hades and lady Persephone – Hadestown invites audiences on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Inspired by traditions of classic American folk music and vintage New Orleans jazz, Mitchell’s beguiling sung-through musical pits industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love.

events.title: DSSO Masterworks 5 – In Sacred Light
events.description: A kaleidoscope of perspectives: “My Country ‘Tis of Thee”, filtered through Charles Ives’ shifting lenses. Fragments of a brilliant Schubert symphony left mysteriously unfinished. An old Lutheran hymn refracted and retold by Bach. A journey from light to darkness and back again, pieced together from a mosaic of sacred texts. Tonight’s program represents the American ideal of individual voices converging into one, unified whole. events.title: Castle Danger Game Night
events.description: Castle Danger Game Nights Every Wednesday | 5:00 – 8:30pm Looking for a fun and welcoming way to spend your Wednesday evenings? Join us at Castle Danger Brewery for Game Nights. Game Nights bring people together to laugh, relax, and share good company over a table of cards, boards, or dice. Our taproom game collection will be open for everyone to use, ranging from classics to modern favorites. Guests are also encouraged to bring their own games to share with the group. Whether you’re coming with friends or flying solo, there’s always a place at the table. Game Nights are all about connection, laughter, and a relaxed community vibe, paired with your favorite Castle Danger beer. Come as you are, stay as long as you’d like, and let’s play!
